subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: This controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and fallback plus auth-provider routing are compatibility- and security-sensitive in this repo.

options.title: Require live proof and fail closed
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and choose fail-closed or equivalent visible operator behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split proof from fallback UX
options.body: Close the OAuth propagation part only after live proof, then track fallback visibility as a narrower policy issue.

options.title: Accept logged fallback
options.body: Allow current fallback behavior after source proof, accepting that operators must inspect logs for auth-route loss.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and fail closed
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and choose fail-closed or equivalent visible operator behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-surface history across auth storage, OpenAI provider identity, Codex owner context, and the relevant security boundary.
